Consider the following statements:
1. The Tenth World Hindi Conference (Vishwa Hindi Sammelan) was held in the year 2015 at Bhopal.
2. The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2018 at Port Louis (Mauritius).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Eighth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2007 at New York.
2. The Fifth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1996 at London.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following pairs of a State/Union Territory and the Region in which it is placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is NOT correctly matched?

options.B: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu — Region 'B'

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 345 from Article 347 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 345 empowers the Legislature of a State to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of that State, while Article 347 empowers the President to direct that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes
options.B: Article 345 deals with the recognition of a language on a direction of the President, while Article 347 deals with the official language of a State
options.C: Both the Articles deal only with the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Article 345 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 347 deals with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage

q: A Hindi-speaking passenger approaches the enquiry counter of a railway station with a query and the railway staff at the counter attend to him only in English. The correct position is that the staff should, as far as possible, attend to him:

options.A: Only in English, enquiries being official work
options.C: Only in the regional language of the State
options.D: After calling an interpreter from the Rajbhasha section

q: A Central Government office issues a notification in English only, on the ground that the persons concerned are all English-knowing officers. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the notification is required to be issued in:

options.A: English only, as issued by the office
options.D: English, with a Hindi summary attached at the end

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India does not declare any language as the national language of India.
2. After the amendment of the Official Languages Act in 1967, English continues to be used for the official purposes of the Union as an associate official language, in addition to Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Maithili language is mainly spoken in the Mithila region of the State of Bihar.
2. The Dogri language is mainly spoken in the Kashmir valley.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttarakhand.
2. Besides Uttarakhand, Sanskrit has also been declared as the second official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Memorandum" is Gyapan.
2. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Office Memorandum" is Karyalaya Gyapan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 346 of the Constitution, the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes shall be the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another.
2. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26th January, 1965.
2. The Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules were framed in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Of the 30 members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, 20 are drawn from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was constituted in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
2. World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Haryana is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Karnataka is placed in Region 'B'.

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Rajasthan is placed in Region 'A'.

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Chhattisgarh is Hindi.

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Nagaland is English.
2. The official language of the State of Meghalaya is English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Bihar.
2. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttar Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Tamil was the first language to be declared a 'classical language' by the Government of India.
2. Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. Marathi is the third most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
2. Telugu is the fourth most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in the year 1954.
2. International Mother Language Day is observed every year on 21st February.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The first Hindi daily newspaper, 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', was published in the year 1854 from Calcutta.
2. 'Alam Ara', the first Indian talkie film released in the year 1931, was made in the Hindi language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Hans' was founded by Munshi Premchand.
2. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was first published in the year 1910.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The real name of Munshi Premchand, the celebrated Hindi novelist, was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava.
2. The first recipient of the Jnanpith Award, in the year 1965, was G. Sankara Kurup.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

1. The first Hindi writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was Sumitranandan Pant.
2. The first woman writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was Ashapurna Devi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. 'Pariksha Guru' (1882), regarded as the first novel in Hindi, was written by Lala Srinivas Das.
2. 'Indumati', published in the year 1900 and regarded as the first short story in Hindi, was written by Kishorilal Goswami.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Kashmiri language belongs to the Dardic group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages.
2. The Santhali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to the Austroasiatic (Munda) family of languages.

Consider the following statements:
1. Marathi does not belong to the Dravidian family of languages.
2. The Bhojpuri language belongs to the Bihari group of languages/dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Bagheli dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
2. The Chhattisgarhi dialect belongs to the Western Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Assamese language belongs to the Eastern group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages.
2. The Sanskrit language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, has no separate script of its own and is generally written in the Devanagari script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

1. The Gujarati script, though derived from Devanagari, has the headstroke (shirorekha) like the Devanagari script.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the expression "Central Government office" includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is referred to in Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

1. The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year 1960.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 5 from Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 5 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 7 deals with the rule-making power of the Central Government
options.B: Section 5 provides that the Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi, while Section 7 provides for the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court, on authorisation by the Governor with the previous consent of the President
options.C: Both the Sections deal only with the documents to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: Section 5 deals with the use of Hindi in judgments of High Courts, while Section 7 deals with the authoritative Hindi text of Central Acts

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 348 from Article 349 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 348 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 349 deals with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with the official language of the States
options.C: Article 348 lays down that the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the authoritative texts of Bills, Acts, orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws, shall be English until Parliament by law otherwise provides, while Article 349 lays down a special procedure for the enactment of certain laws relating to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Article 348 empowers the President to direct the recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State, while Article 349 empowers a State Legislature to adopt the official language of the State

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Central Translation Bureau?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material, while the Central Translation Bureau conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya
options.B: Both the bodies only conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.C: Both the bodies function only at the level of Zonal Railways
options.D: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya for employees who cannot attend regular classes and prepared the standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani), while the Central Translation Bureau is mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the World Hindi Conferences is FALSE?

options.A: The First World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1975 at Nagpur
options.B: The Second World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1976 at Port Louis (Mauritius)
options.C: The Tenth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2015 at Bhopal
options.D: The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2018 at New Delhi

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the committees for the implementation of the Official Language Policy is FALSE?

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of 30 members
options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister
options.C: The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the District Magistrate of the town

q: A Central Government office finalises tender forms and a notice inviting tenders and proposes to issue them in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that tender forms and notices inviting tenders are required to be issued in:

options.A: Hindi only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: A Central Government office has to issue a licence (permit) to an applicant and proposes to issue it in English only, on the ground that the applicant is an English-knowing firm. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the licence or permit is required to be issued in:

options.A: English only, as proposed by the office
options.C: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: An Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi is translated into Hindi, and the translation is published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, that translation shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A mere unofficial summary of the Act
options.B: The authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

q: A substantial proportion of the population of a State desires that a language spoken by them should be recognised by the State. The President is satisfied in this regard and directs that the language shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes in a part of that State. This direction is issued under:

At a railway station, announcements for the guidance of passengers are made only in Hindi and English, the regional language of the area being omitted altogether. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that such announcements are required to be made in:

options.A: Hindi and English only, as is being done at the station
options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 67 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 57 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 91 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 92 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi typewriting examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award

q: An employee aged 43 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

q: In a Central Government office, 88 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 15,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976

q:

Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 6 from Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 6 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 7 vests the rule-making power in the Central Government
options.B: Section 6 provides that a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi, while Section 7 provides for the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court, on authorisation by the Governor with the previous consent of the President

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 346 from Article 347 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 346 empowers the President to direct the recognition of a language, while Article 347 deals with communication between the Union and a State

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Central Hindi Training Institute?
